description_en: A group of 14 stone memorial pillars dating approximately from the 14th to the 16th century is located in the hamlet of Umgāḍ, at the junction with the Karnali Highway, in the Jumla district of Nepal. The pillars are arranged in a southwest to northeast axis along a small road. Umgāḍ is situated about 100 meters away from the right bank of the Karnali River and 4 km west of Jumla Khalanga, the district headquarters. The hamlet of Umgāḍ is relatively new, as historical photographs from 1967 show that the area was previously occupied by rice fields.During the first archaeological survey conducted in the 1990s by Dominique Baudais, a total of 16 pillars were recorded. However, due to road widening and ongoing construction activities, four pillars have been lost, and some of the remaining pillars have suffered significant damage, with pillar 001 being particularly affected. The carvings on the pillars have also weathered over time and are highly eroded.Stone memorial pillars were commonly erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th centuries. These pillars were built to commemorate deceased individuals, many of whom were warriors. In Umgāḍ, some of the pillars depict horse riders, which are often interpreted as representations of warriors (pillars 004, 005, 006, 011) (Andolfatto 2019). Religious architecture is also depicted on some pillars, such as stupa-like structures (pillars 011 and 012). Additionally, most of the pillars feature traditional representations of astral bodies, including the sun, moon, and stars, at their tops.According to Dilli Raj Sharma, two of the pillars are dated to the year ŚS 1423 CE (1501 AD) (Sharma 2012, p. 183). These may correspond to pillars 004 and 005. One of the inscriptions on these pillars reads "sakunamālā puṇyākrit putra suvaṃ," which can be translated as "on the pious work of Sakunmālā, may her son be well."

historical_events.event_description: Inscription of four or more lines at the basis of pillar 004.According to Dilli Raj Sharma, the inscription bears the date ŚS 1423 (1501 AD) (Sharma 2012, p. 183). According to the same author, this pillar, or pillar 005 inscription's reads the following:sakunamālā puṇyākrit putra suvaṃ, translated as 'on the pious work of Sakunmālā (her) son be well'.
